- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 and prices drop sharply, model often fails to capture the reversal; adjust downward by 2–5% in the following 3–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and prices are volatile, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch early reversal or rebound.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 65–70 range after 10+ days of volatility, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment history shows recent “1.00” followed by “-0.33” or “0.00”, model often misreads sentiment shift; adjust forecast downward 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- In absence of official event context, assume sentiment is “neutral” unless recent sentiment is >0.67 or <0.33; apply default correction of -1% if sentiment is 0.00–0.33.
